:::{#exm-finite-additivity}
#### Counting elements is finitely additive

For the die rolls $D = \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$ ([sets of die rolls](sets-functions.qmd#exm-set)),
let $\measure(A) \eqdef \abs{A}$, the number of elements of $A$
([cardinality](sets-functions.qmd#def-finite-set)),
for each set $A$ in the $\sigma$-algebra of all subsets of $D$
(@exm-sigma-algebra).
The sets $\set{1, 2}$ and $\set{5, 6}$ are pairwise disjoint
(@exm-pairwise-disjoint), and:

$$
\ba
\measure(\set{1, 2} \cup \set{5, 6})
&= \measure(\set{1, 2, 5, 6})
&& \text{(take the union)} \\
&= 4
&& \text{(count the elements)} \\
&= 2 + 2
&& \text{(write 4 as a sum)} \\
&= \measure(\set{1, 2}) + \measure(\set{5, 6})
&& \text{(count each set's elements)}
\ea
$$

The same holds for any pairwise disjoint sets,
because the sizes of disjoint sets add,
so $\measure$ is finitely additive.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-finitely-additive}
#### Squaring the count is not finitely additive

On the same $\sigma$-algebra, let $\measureb(A) \eqdef \abs{A}^2$.
The sets $\set{1}$ and $\set{2}$ are pairwise disjoint, but

$$
\ba
\measureb(\set{1} \cup \set{2})
&= \measureb(\set{1, 2})
&& \text{(take the union)} \\
&= 2^2 \\
&= 4,
&& \text{(count, then square)} \\
\measureb(\set{1}) + \measureb(\set{2})
&= 1^2 + 1^2 \\
&= 2,
&& \text{(count each set, then square)}
\ea
$$

and $4 \ne 2$, so $\measureb$ is not finitely additive.

:::
